_about: World map (real-time like DF). Coordinates are game pixels on the 320x180 screen. Values are a starting point only: balance comes later.

time._note: day_seconds = real seconds per in-game day at speed x1 · speeds = keys 1/2/3

rules._note: move_speed px/day along roads · max_troops = cap when there are no ranks (see ranks) · regen = troops/day for a general resting in its own castle · ai_think_days = how often the AI looks for a target

council._note: Every `every_days` the map stops for a council (like DF): troops come into each side's reserve and are handed to generals standing in their own castles. income = troops per owned castle per council (+capital_bonus for the capital) · start = reserve at the start of the war · step = troops per click. regen_per_day in rules is 0 now: troops only come back through the council. Basic values, balance later.

_council_actions: Each general standing in its own castle gets ONE action per council: levy = +council.levy troops into the reserve, persuade a prisoner (see prisoners), raise the castle's wall one level (once per castle per council) or build a siege engine (see siege). Handing out troops (step buttons) is free.

prisoners._note: capture_if_fell = chance a beaten general is taken when its general fell in battle (pulling out before the duel = never; no way home = always). Persuade chance = base + per_council x councils captive - (loyalty - 50) x loyalty_weight (+king_bonus if the king asks), clamped to min..max. Kings never join. default_loyalty for generals without "loyalty" (kings 100). joined_loyalty = loyalty after joining. Basic values, balance later.

siege._note: Walls and siege engines (council actions, one per general like levy). wall_max = highest wall level · wall_take_per_level = damage the troops defending their own castle take less per level (0.1 = -10%; not the general, not the duel; road battles have no walls) · wall_lost_on_capture = levels knocked off when a castle changes hands · engines = false turns engines off · engine_speed = march speed x while dragging one · engine_cancels = wall levels an engine cuts in a battle at a walled castle (then it is spent, won or lost; a castle with no wall leaves it for the next; it is lost too if its general is beaten on a road) · ai_engine_wall = the AI builds an engine when a next-door enemy castle has this wall or more · castle_background = battle ground for castle battles. A castle may set "wall" to start with (default 0). Basic values, balance later.

growth._note: General levels (like DF). Every battle gives both generals EXP: per_troop x enemy troops they beat + win or lose (+fell_general when the enemy general fell, on the field or in the duel). EXP from level L to L+1 = exp_to_next.base + exp_to_next.per_level x (L-1). Each level above 1 adds per_level to the general's battle numbers: hp = its HP, atk = its hits and duel blows, special = its specials' damage (0.05 = +5% per level). Level 1 = battle_config.json as it is. A general may set "level" (default 1). Basic values, balance later.

ranks._note: General ranks (like DF): the rank caps the troops a general leads (max_troops per rank, lowest first; rules.max_troops is used only without ranks). level_needed = level a general must reach before it can be promoted to that rank. Promotion is the KING's council action (one per council, instead of levy / persuade / ...), for any free general of its side wherever it is; it adds reward_loyalty. The AI king promotes the highest-level general that can be, unless a prisoner would join with ai_persuade_first chance or more if the king asked. A general may set "rank" (index, default 0; kings default to the top rank). Max troops stay at 30 or less: formations have 30 spots. Basic values, balance later.

map_sprites._note: Marching armies are drawn with the battle sprite of their troops (battle_config.json sprites). Per side: sprite id, scale on the map, followers = extra troops walking behind (one per `per` troops, at most `max`). A general can set its own "unit" to override. The ring at the feet is the side colour (a captured general who joins keeps its own look but the colour tells the side).
